policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'They spend their days in prosperity' fits both the qere יְכַלּוּ (כלה, complete/spend) and the ketiv יבלו (בלה, wear out/use up); ASV renders the same idiom with בלה at Job 36:11 as 'spend their days in prosperity', so 'spend' does not distinguish the readings. No textual note on the verse. Base qere fallback carries the projection.

ASV 'Let his own eyes see his destruction' renders a plural noun, matching the qere עֵינָיו 'his eyes'; the ketiv עינו reads as singular 'his eye', which the English wording excludes. No textual note on the verse.
